name: vehicle-traffic
description: Chapter 2: Add 4 haulers with drivers, converge 3 of them on one tile. Finding #21: TrafficJamEvent never actually fires here, at any tick budget — a direct engine trace confirms why: the redirect happens only 5 ticks after the initial move commands, nowhere near enough travel time from the shared vehicle spawn point to reach the 3 separate staging tiles first, so all 3 vehicles travel in perfect lockstep the whole way and arrive together with no contention. detectTrafficJam (EventEngine.ts) also requires TRAFFIC_JAM_MIN_VEHICLES=3 vehicles simultaneously in the 'waiting' state on the same target tile for TRAFFIC_JAM_MIN_TICKS=10+ ticks; with only 3 vehicles converging (1 occupies the tile, at most 2 can ever be blocked waiting on it), that threshold is structurally out of reach regardless of timing — a real jam would need a 4th vehicle also converging on the same point. This file exercises real vehicle pathing/redirection but does not exercise TrafficJamEvent; assertions reflect that.

steps.description: Plain new_game at the sandbox default. The `cash:150000` bump that used to sit here has moved to `campaign start` below, which is the step that actually decides this scenario's cash.

campaign start replaces the whole GameState (createGameForLevel), cash included, so `cash:` belongs here and nowhere earlier. $150,000 covers 4 drivers ($800 each) plus 4 tier-1 debris haulers ($25,000 each) = $103,200, which is what the convergence test itself needs: 4 vehicles bought through 4 enabled dealership rows, not 1 bought and 3 overdrawn.

expect.note: the cash: override replaces dusty_hollow's $50,000 default outright

steps.description: Opens the Fleet panel and buys hauler #1 by clicking its tier-1 dealership row. The three buys below reuse the open panel.

Hauler #2, bought by clicking the same dealership row again: $121,800 in hand against $25,000. awaitUsable is the affordability assertion -- FleetPanel disables a tier row on cash < purchaseCost, so an underfunded run fails here instead of buying anyway.
Hauler #3, same row again: $96,800 in hand against $25,000.
Hauler #4, same row again: $71,800 in hand against $25,000. Fourth and last, and the fleet the move commands below converge.

No events fired." — no TrafficJamEvent, for the reasons in the file's top-level description. No scalar field exists to assert the negative directly (pendingEvent isn't in SerializableGameState), so this anchors on the one thing that IS externally checkable: the fleet stays at 4, undisturbed.
